liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Shakedown Street is good but not over the top; Show opened with Shakedown Street, with Jerry in shape and leading after a week of California coast shows [13][16]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha ends in an unusual segue into Women Are Smarter [21]
- **Man Smart (Woman Smarter)** (1 review): Reviewer's first of this song, which closed the first set [14]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Not Fade Away is fast-paced for the era, with Phil's playing driving it [21]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Phil's work from the Not Fade Away intro through Stella Blue is the show's standout stretch [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-02-21.151136.aud.lohr.vernon.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 155 min [1]
- **gd1982-02-21.148007.sbd.miller.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1982-02-21.149024.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 151 min [4]
- **gd82-02-21.sbd.dodd.16247.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 145 min; rated 3.26/5 by 19 [7]. Said about its sound: Sounds good but somewhat flat, a common issue with early-80s shows, though better than many; Mix is light on bass, in the reviewer's view; Weir's guitar tone stands out on the recording, compressed yet glowing, with highlighted accents and phrases [15][16][17][19]
- **gd1982-02-21.154099.2nd.set.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 10 songs; 80 min [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was a high school senior who brought books and did homework during the show [14]
- After Brokedown Palace the band left, then returned for a second encore of Casey Jones [20]
- Only a couple hundred people remained; Bob's speaker blew during Brokedown and rattled through Casey [20]
- Reviewer likes the early-80s band: renewed energy after the late-70s break, combined with long-seasoned playing together [12]
- After this show and the Warfield shows, the reviewer gained new appreciation for the 1982 year [13]
- Second set is solid and tight but a notch below the first set [13]
- Framed as a hometown show following a three-night Greek stand [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-02-21.151136.aud.lohr.vernon.flac2496**: taped by Gesine Lohr; transferred by Matt Vernon; source: Nak CM700 > TC-D5 > MAC > This copy [1]
- **gd1982-02-21.148007.sbd.miller.clugston.flac16**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > Dat (16/44.1) [3]. Also: Transfer by Charlie Miller; Gregg Nixon's unknown audience source patches 35 seconds of Bird Song; A Beyer M88 audience source from Tompkins and Stankiewicz supplies the crowd and most of China Cat Sunflower, plus small patches [3]
- **gd1982-02-21.149024.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; 3 x Nakamichi 700 cardioids (center mic 6db EQ), X/Y 85 degrees > Sony D5 (20' left of center, 35-40' from… [4]. Also: A Miller soundboard source patches Bird Song and Drums; a Beyer M88 source supplies crowd and China Cat start [4]
- **gd82-02-21.sbd.dodd.16247.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [7]. Also: Soundboard to cassette, DAT, CDR, then EAC and shntool to shn, by Ernie Dodd; discs from Mark Horvath [7]
- **gd1982-02-21.154099.2nd.set.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5 (Maxell XLII-S 90) [8]. Also: Mark Severson's Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 47-second patch in Drums [8]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Pauley Pavilion - February 21, 1982](https://www.dead.net/show/february-21-1982) [24]
